title: Citizen participation: oversight that multiplies transparency
excerpt: When citizens can check the progress of public works in their area, oversight is no longer the government's alone; it becomes collective.
content:
When citizens can check the progress of public works in their area, oversight is no longer the government's alone; it becomes collective.

Oversight doesn't scale from the inside alone

No entity has enough supervisors to watch every site every day. But every site has neighbors who walk past it daily. That asymmetry is an opportunity.

What enabling participation means

  • Publish the actual progress of public works in the area.
  • Let citizens submit observations linked to a specific project.
  • Close the loop: every observation gets a traceable response.

Transparency that can't be consulted isn't transparency; it's just publication.

The conditions for success

Participation requires understandable information. Publishing a budget certificate and a contract number informs no one. Publishing "this road, this progress, this expected date, this evidence" does. Data quality determines whether the mechanism is used or abandoned.

The side effect

When contractors know their progress is public, reporting quality improves without the need for penalties. Visibility is, in itself, an incentive.
